Collaboration Progress Monitor 2025/26

How well are UK universities and businesses working together?

The Collaboration Progress Monitor (CPM) tracks the health of university–business collaboration across the UK. Built by the National Centre for Universities and Business (NCUB), it brings together HESA HE-BCI data, economic context and institution-level analysis into one evidence base — extending Chapter 1 of the State of the Relationship.

Tab 3

The CPM framework: four categories, 13+ measures

The R&I Collaboration Progress Monitor provides a systematic, evidence-based view of university–business collaboration across the UK. Three established pillars cover engagement volume, financial investment and commercial outputs — and the fourth pillar, now live with its first metrics, uses UKRI's Gateway to Research (GtR) to capture publicly funded collaborative R&D at the project level.

Collaboration activity 01
2 measures

Counts the volume of formal interactions between UK universities and business, distinguishing SMEs (under 250 employees) from large businesses.

  1. Total interactions with SMEs
  2. Total interactions with large business
Investment in collaboration 02
8 measures

Tracks the financial flows that underpin collaborative R&D: income from business partnerships, industry contributions to HE research spend, and Innovate UK grant funding.

  1. Business collaboration income
  2. % of HE collaboration income from business
  3. Domestic industry funds in HE R&D
  4. Overseas industry funds in HE R&D
  5. Income from interactions with SMEs
  6. Income from interactions with large business
  7. Total Innovate UK grants
  8. Income per Innovate UK grant
Products of collaboration 03
3 measures

Captures tangible commercial outputs: licensed intellectual property, licensing income earned, and active spinout companies formed from HE research.

  1. Number of licences granted
  2. Total licensing income
  3. Academic spinouts
R&D collaboration (GtR) 04 LIVE
13 measures · 3 dimensions

Built from UKRI's Gateway to Research: every publicly funded R&I project with a business partner, linked to universities, funders and mechanisms.

  1. Volume & scale — V1–V6: links, partners, projects, total and mean grant value
  2. Intensity & productivity — I1–I3, I5a, I6a: collaborations per university and per business, multi-university businesses, KTP and Collaborative R&D project counts
  3. Innovation depth — D6, D7: associated publications and further funding leveraged

How the four pillars connect

Each pillar measures a different stage of the same relationship: activity creates the pipeline, investment fuels it, GtR captures the publicly co-funded core, and products are what comes out the other end.

Why add a GtR pillar?

HE-BCI captures income flowing into universities, but says little about the structure of collaboration. Gateway to Research lists every UKRI-funded project together with its participating organisations, so it can show who collaborates with whom, on what, and how partnership networks evolve. It also covers collaboration that generates no direct HE income — in-kind partnerships, consortium membership and co-created research agendas — that the current monitor misses. Linking GtR organisation identifiers to Companies House would additionally allow the monitor to profile the size, sector and geography of partner firms.

Indicator scorecard

Computed from the panel · hover a cell for the underlying numbers
⏫ 10%+ above baseline ⌃ 1–10% above — within ±1% ⌄ 1–10% below ⏬ 10%+ below baseline
Benchmarks: annual change (2024/25 vs 2023/24), short-term (2024/25 vs five-year average), long-term (2024/25 vs ten-year average), pre-Covid (2024/25 vs 2018/19). All income measures in constant prices.

How concentrated is business collaboration income?

A Pareto-style curve: providers are ranked from highest to lowest, then plotted as cumulative share of total income (y) against cumulative share of providers (x). A 45° line would mean perfectly equal distribution; the further the curve sits above it, the more concentrated the income. Reference markers show the share captured by the top 10%, 20% and 50% of providers. Latest year, constant prices.

Spinouts and the capital behind them

CPM-defined spinouts surviving 3+ years (bars) and total estimated external investment in active spinouts (line) — real 2024/25 prices or nominal cash, per the switch above. The dashed horizontal reference line is the all-time average of external investment (on the same real or nominal basis) across the panel's 11 years — useful for spotting years that run above or below the long-run norm. "Spinouts" here = Spin-outs with some HE provider ownership + Other spin-outs. One anomalous investment return (>£20bn, single provider-year 2022/23) excluded from the investment total; it remains in provider views and exports.

Spinout employment — total and per-provider median

FTE across CPM-defined spin-outs
Total spinout employment (bars, left axis) and the median FTE per provider among those reporting any spinout employment (line, right axis). FTE sum across the two CPM spin-out categories (Spin-outs with HE ownership + Other spin-outs), active firms surviving 3+ years. Source: HESA table-4e.

Spinouts, staff and student start-ups — distinct categories

All surviving 3+ years
The CPM report measures Spinouts as the two HESA categories with an institutional ownership link (Spin-outs with some HE provider ownership + Other spin-outs). Staff start-ups and Student start-ups (sometimes called "graduate start-ups") are reported alongside but conceptually different: staff retain their academic post while running a company, and student start-ups emerge from the student body rather than from institutional IP. All three series are counts of firms still active after three or more years. Source: HESA table-4e.

Five-year compound annual growth, by cluster

Share of providers in each growth band, based on the compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the latest five years (2019/20 → 2024/25), smoothing out short-term ups and downs. Providers below a minimum 2019/20 base (£100k for income measures; 10 for counts) excluded. Income measures in constant prices. Hover for provider counts.

The full distribution

Every eligible provider's five-year CAGR for the selected metric, by cluster. Box = interquartile range.

Reading this page

The CAGR shows the average yearly rate at which a measure has increased or decreased over five years. Significant means 10%+ a year in either direction; moderate is 3–10%; stable is within ±3%. Because income is lumpy and contract-driven, smaller providers swing between bands more readily — compare with the funnel plot on the Overview sub-tab. Switch metrics above to see how growth patterns differ between income, engagement volumes and commercialisation.

How each stream contributed to BCI growth

Decomposed growth: each stream's contribution to the total BCI change between and , in percentage points. Computed as (component weight in base year) × (component % change). The sum of the contributions equals the total BCI % change. Constant 2024/25 prices.

BCI and its components, absolute

Total BCI (line) and the four component streams stacked beneath. £m, constant 2024/25 prices. Reflects the group selected above.

Percent change since first year (indexed)

Every series rebased to 100 in the first available year — easier to compare growth trajectories when component sizes differ. Values above 100 mean growth; below 100, decline.

In production

This pillar is being developed for the next release. Planned measures include degree apprenticeships co-delivered with employers, placement and internship volumes, CPD learner days, graduate retention in partner businesses, and co-designed curriculum activity. If you'd like to shape these metrics, get in touch with the NCUB research team.

Talent pipelines

Degree apprenticeships, placements and internships brokered between universities and employers.

Workforce development

CPD and continuing education delivered to business — learner days already appear in HE-BCI and will seed this pillar.

Graduate flows

Where graduates go: retention in collaborating firms, regional retention, and progression into R&D roles.

Want the full set?

This view shows the bundled starter dataset of NCUB success stories. To pull the full corpus (~hundreds of case studies) from ncub.co.uk/insights, run:

pip install requests beautifulsoup4
python fetch_case_studies.py

The scraper writes case_studies.json (picked up automatically by the build) plus case_study_review.csv for hand-correcting any rows where heuristic extraction missed the university or business partner. See the README for full instructions.
